verdict.rationale: Fellow's own Developer API covers much of the core UI data. It can list and read notes, recordings and transcripts, write, prepend, append and find-replace agenda content in round-tripping Fellow Markdown, mark action items complete or archive them, upload recordings, and let super admins export and delete data. However, nothing documents UI parity, and many UI features have no API equivalent in the evidence: recording and retention policies, keyword tracking, transcript redaction, bot customization, Ask Fellow, and MCP governance. Note deletion is also restricted to super admins. Missing for 10: documented UI/API parity claim, API coverage of workspace settings, recording and retention policies, redaction, keyword tracking and Ask Fellow, creating action items, non-admin note deletion, a published OpenAPI spec (probe returned 404), and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: The Developer API opens that data to you: transcripts, structured notes, and more, all available through standard REST calls.
Write a note's agenda and/or rename the note. Provide `content_fellow_markdown`, `title`, or both.
The format round-trips: the `content_fellow_markdown` you read from a note is exactly what you can send back to `POST /note/{id}/agenda`.
Mark an action item as complete or incomplete.
Upload a recording from a URL. Use this endpoint to bring an existing meeting recording into Fellow.
Only users with super admin privileges can delete notes through the API.
